content: 1. If you have created an account but cannot log in, it is because your request must first be approved by an administrator. This process can take up to 24 hours after you sign up. Please wait for the approval before attempting to log in again. 2. If you cannot see the sidebar on the microchapter assigned to you, ensure that you have created a template page for your chapter and inserted it into the chapter's page. For example, if your chapter is Diabetes Mellitus, create a new page titled Template:Diabetes Mellitus. Copy the template code from Template:XYZ, paste it into your new page, and replace XYZ with Diabetes Mellitus in all commands. Save the page, and the sidebar will appear on the right-hand side of the respective page. 3. To upload an image to your chapter, click Upload a picture or File at the bottom of any page. Follow the steps to upload the image. Then, go to the page where you want the image to appear, click edit source, place the cursor where you want the image, and insert the appropriate code. 4. To hyperlink a term, select the term, press Ctrl+K (or click the hyperlink button in visual edit), and choose the corresponding page from the options provided. If you cannot hyperlink a term, it may be because a page for that term does not exist or the terminology you used does not match existing pages. Adjust the terminology to match existing pages. 5. If inserting an image causes the page footer (e.g., References heading) to appear improperly formatted, edit the source, place the cursor below the image command, and insert the appropriate code to fix the formatting. 6. To generate a reference from a DOI, click Editors Help Menu at the bottom of any page, navigate to How to Edit A Page, and select References. Then, click DOI Wikipedia reference generator, paste the DOI address, and click load. 7. To generate a reference from a URL, click Editors Help Menu, go to How to Edit A Page, and select References. Then, click Wikipedia template filling, paste the URL, select URL from the dropdown menu, check Add ref tag, and click submit. This will generate a reference code for use. 8. To create redirects for your chapter, search for the synonym (e.g., Alport syndrome) in the main search box. If the page does not exist, click create the page and type `redirect [Target Page]` in the edit box. Save the page to complete the redirect. 9. To report epidemiology in the Epidemiology and Demographics section, express the data as a rate per 100,000 individuals. For example, if 2 individuals per 100 are affected, convert this to 2,000 per 100,000. 10. The Patient Information section should be written at an eighth-grade reading level, avoiding medical jargon and complex terms. Use resources like the CDC website to simplify information for patients. 11. The Diagnostic Study of Choice section should include the gold standard test for diagnosing the disease. If clinical criteria are the gold standard, include those criteria in this section. 12. References should be inserted at the end of a sentence, after the full stop. 13. The overview section should not include references. Instead, references should be listed in the explanatory content. 14. The Differential Diagnosis section should list all possible differential diagnoses based on the clinical presentation of the disease. 15. The Resident Survival Guide is a guideline-based approach to managing common medical emergencies. It includes algorithms for disease recognition and management based on published guidelines. 16. To create an animated GIF for images, download and save the image to your computer. Use a program like Paint to mark abnormalities on one copy of the image while keeping another unmarked. Upload both images to a GIF-making website, set the animation speed to 2400 milliseconds, and download the GIF. Upload the GIF to your chapter as you would an image. 17. If no published primary or secondary prevention methods exist for a disease, do not leave the section blank. Use the template statement: There are no established measures of prevention for [disease]. 18. Template statements for your chapter can be found in the designated section of the WikiDoc platform.
